edits.context: emergencyPhrases — "En voi hyvin" / "I don't feel well"
edits.reason: Direct Russian calque from 'Я плохо себя чувствую'. 'жаман сезіну' is colloquial and Russian-influenced; native Kazakh prefers 'нашар сезіну'. Progressive form 'сезініп тұрмын' is more natural for describing a current state to a stranger (e.g. doctor). Pronoun 'мен' is implicit in conjugation and can be dropped for naturalness in a short distress phrase.

edits.before: Такси — жүргізушіге өз бағаңды ұсынуға болады
edits.after: Такси — жүргізушіге өз бағаңызды ұсынуға болады
edits.reason: Register inconsistency: 'бағаңды' uses 2nd person singular informal possessive, but every other app description and the emergency phrases use the formal 2nd person ('-ңыз' suffix, e.g. 'сақтаңыз', 'жүктеп алыңыз'). Changed to formal 'бағаңызды'.

considered_but_kept.note: 'төтенше' is the official term used in 'Төтенше жағдайлар министрлігі'. 'Бірыңғай шұғыл нөмір' would be slightly more idiomatic for 112 but current form is acceptable and clear.
Could take accusative ('Жедел жәрдемді шақырыңыз') but indefinite nominative is idiomatic in Kazakh imperative for generic emergency services. Both forms are used.
Literally 'I don't know Russian' but this is the standard idiomatic way Kazakh speakers say 'I don't speak Russian'. 'Сөйлемеймін' would be more literal but less natural.
Style guide mentions 'жоғалдым' but 'адасып қалдым' is the more natural phrase for getting lost while traveling. Kept as-is.
Correct copular form. Could also be 'Мен фин азаматымын' (I'm a Finnish citizen) but short form fits the emergency-phrase style.

uncertainties: Whether to formalize 'Жалпы төтенше нөмір' to 'Бірыңғай шұғыл нөмір' — left conservative.
Whether 'Жедел жәрдем шақырыңыз' should take accusative case — both forms exist in usage.
